## /rebar-debug report — the fix is ALREADY LANDED; this ticket was never written up or closed

**Step 0 finding.** This bug's fix merged on 2026-08-26 as Gerrit change **2236**, commit
`73c45f16cfe2` ("fix(review-bot): drop superseded revisions", `rebar-ticket: daa7-e840-19b9-4851`,
`Change-Id: I20a268b23ec1d0aabc51dc6888ef35c6fe6d5338`), submitted 10:47:05Z and an ancestor of
`origin/main`. The ticket kept zero comments and unchecked criteria only because the session that
landed it never wrote back. NO new code change was required; this pass re-verified the landed fix
from scratch and closes the record.

**Proven root cause (preexisting omission; cited).** `app._worker` did
`event = await queue.get()` and went straight to `_voter.review_and_vote(...)` with nothing
between the dequeue and the review re-reading the change's current revision. With
`WORKER_COUNT = 1` (`src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:80`) and reviews taking 15-45 minutes, a queued
event is routinely obsolete when it runs. The capability existed but was never asked on this
path: `GerritClient.get_change_event` has queried `?o=CURRENT_REVISION` since inception, scoped
by its docstring to the manual `/rerun` path only. Origin is `1d1a072a75c7`
("S4b (918c): review-bot receiver logic + LLM-Review voter + backfill", story
`918c-589a-fc4a-4c52` cogent-strut-kid) — the same origin bug `baa8-6a40-7052-46c2` cited. Live
evidence: changes 2226/2231/2232 voted consistently one patchset behind (PS7 uploaded 05:59:01,
vote landed on PS6 at 06:10:12).

**Which guarantee, and why BOTH are needed.** A dequeue-time check alone only NARROWS the window
— a patchset can land between the check and the vote. The complete answer is two guards, and
both are now on `main`:

1. **"Don't start"** — this ticket (2236). `_superseded_by` in `_worker` discards a superseded
   event BEFORE any clone/LLM spend. This is the one that saves money and drains the `in_flight`
   gauge sooner, which is the deploy-deferral link to `7b4a` / ADR `a45f`.
2. **"Don't publish a vote"** — bug `baa8-6a40-7052-46c2` (curvaceous-powellite-foal, closed),
   Gerrit 2330 / `afe01efaa8b2`. `voter._review_and_vote` re-reads the current revision
   immediately before `post_review` and SUPPRESSES the vote when the reviewed revision is no
   longer current. That is the guard that actually CLOSES the TOCTOU race, and it is the one
   that matters for correctness (a stale vote's Gerrit comment triggers g2p's `recheck=verify`
   mapping, whose Change-Id-keyed `cancel-in-progress` cancelled the current patchset's Verified
   run).

Neither guard can silently drop live work: both FAIL OPEN on an unreadable current revision, and
both exempt forced / `manual-rerun` events, which are built from the current revision by
construction.

**Re-verification (worktree at `origin/main` 565e1856bc9d, `.venv` + `[reviewbot]` extra, so
fastapi is present and the tests RUN rather than skip).**

    tests/unit/test_review_bot.py + test_review_bot_stale_vote_baa8.py -> 113 passed
    make lint            -> clean
    make typecheck       -> Success: no issues found in 684 source files
    check_complexity_baseline.py --check -> active=39 new=0 increased=0 stale=10

**Non-vacuity.** The discard test's `assert reviewed == []` is anchored: reverting production
`app.py` to `73c45f16cfe2^` makes it fail as `assert ['old_rev'] == []`, proving the harness
genuinely dispatched the event to the reviewer. The assertion is not passing on an empty queue.

**Mutation results — each production behaviour reverted individually; only its own test reddens
(rc checked, each seed confirmed applied):**

| # | seeded mutation | discard | current-rev | fail-open | forced-rerun |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | revert `app.py` to pre-fix (whole guard removed) | **FAIL** | pass | pass | pass |
| M2 | `_superseded_by` fails CLOSED on unknown current | pass | pass | **FAIL** | pass |
| M3 | drop the `force` / `manual-rerun` bypass | pass | pass | pass | **FAIL** |
| M4 | `_discard_superseded` emits no `VOTER_ERROR` marker | **FAIL** | pass | pass | pass |

Every mutant was killed, each by exactly the test that owns that criterion, and no test is a
change-detector for another's behaviour. (A first M4 attempt produced a syntax error rather than
a live mutant — discarded and re-seeded at a line-start anchor, then re-run.)
